verdict: Andrej Karpathy's weekend hack: Claude filtered 43M Hacker News comments from 20 years down to the 6,454 YouTube videos HN keeps recommending, served as a clean, login-free YouTube alternative (state lives in your browser, thumbnails are mid-video frames, plus a 'Longs' tab). Built in about 2 hours with Claude Code and Opus 5.5; the comment-analysis data is a downloadable zip so you can have your own agent build a variant. His Nov 1 launch post passed 50k likes and 42k bookmarks. It's a curated watch list, not a full YouTube replacement: no search across all of YouTube, no subscriptions.
useThisIf: you want smart, ad-free video picks without an algorithm or account, or a real example of what one person can ship with Claude Code in an afternoon.

name: DeepSeek Super-agent
verdict: DeepSeek Harness team's MIT-licensed prototype of a proactive coding agent: a resident Router watches GitHub and chat events and hands work to isolated Workers that reproduce bugs and open PRs on their own, with a design write-up on when the agent should act and when to stay quiet. About 16k GitHub stars within days of its Oct 31 release and wide coverage framing it as DeepSeek's answer to Claude Code. It's labelled a prototype: expect to self-host and wire it up yourself, not a polished product.
useThisIf: you run a repo or dev group chat and want to experiment with an always-on agent that picks up issues without being asked.

name: Open Bot Avatar
verdict: Open-source (MIT) JSON spec plus a zero-dependency renderer for cute animated agent avatars: one SVG shape plus eye positions becomes a character that follows the cursor and switches between idle, thinking and happy states, with a studio of ready-made bots (cat, ghost, mug, star, wizard hat). Dominik Scholz open-sourced it on Nov 2 after his hand-made Grok Bot avatars went viral; the launch post hit ~2k likes and 1.5k bookmarks. A design asset kit, not an app. Ignore the unofficial pump.fun coin some accounts attached to it; it isn't part of the project.
useThisIf: you're building an agent, bot or chat UI and want it to have a friendly animated face without hiring an illustrator.

name: Treg
verdict: One MCP server and one key for 4,100+ agent tools across 123 providers (people search, email enrichment, SEO, ads, social and scraping data) billed per call at the provider's own rate with 0% markup, so you can build lead lists from inside Claude Code or Codex instead of paying for Clay or Apollo seats. The Nov 2 'open-source Clay killer' launch drew ~800 likes and 1k bookmarks; their own example run found 20 verified emails for 27 people for $0.58. Repo is public (superdesigndev/treg) but the license isn't a standard OSI one, and the data calls cost money after a $1 free credit.
useThisIf: you do outbound or GTM work in a coding agent and want pay-as-you-go enrichment instead of a monthly data-tool subscription.

name: Xmind Agent (Xmind 2027)
verdict: Xmind 2027 (launched Oct 28 2026, on Product Hunt Nov 1) adds a chat agent inside the 20-year-old mind-map app: start from a thought, PDF, webpage or YouTube link and refine the map by talking. Also ships an Xmind MCP server and ChatGPT plugin so Claude/ChatGPT can read and edit your maps. Web, desktop and Android now; iOS 'coming soon'. Agent features sit behind Xmind's paid plans beyond the free tier.
useThisIf: you already think in mind maps and want AI to research and restructure them, or want Claude/ChatGPT to work off a map you built.

name: Agent Inbox
verdict: From the Novu team (PH launch Nov 1 2026): one command (npx @agentinbox/cli setup) gives your agent its own email address, Telegram bot and Slack app sharing one inbox. Agents can send updates or ask/approve/choose and block until a human answers; works over CLI or MCP from Claude Code, Cursor, etc. Starts as a no-account free demo; you claim it with login. Useful human-in-the-loop plumbing, but your agent is now emailing real people, so set contact rules first.
useThisIf: your long-running agent needs to ping you for approvals on Telegram/Slack/email instead of waiting in a terminal.

name: Friday
verdict: Free MIT desktop app (macOS/Windows/Linux; PH launch Nov 1 2026) that runs Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Copilot and ~10 more agents side by side on your own plans. A lead agent splits work into a task board, others pick tasks, finished tasks get cross-checked, and when one tool hits its usage limit the task is handed to another with a record of what was done. No account, local only. It doesn't raise anyone's limits; it just routes around them.
useThisIf: you pay for two or more coding agents and keep losing momentum when Claude Code hits its 5-hour limit.

name: agent-desktop (Vercel Labs)
verdict: Apache-2.0 CLI + C library from Vercel Labs for computer use via the OS accessibility tree, not screenshots: snapshot an app, get JSON refs for every clickable element, act on a ref, snapshot again. macOS/Windows/Linux, npm install -g agent-desktop. v1.0.2 shipped Oct 30 2026 and it was #1 on GitHub trending Nov 3 (~2.3K stars in a day, ~9.7K total). Developer tool; snapshots can contain private screen content.
useThisIf: you're building an agent that has to drive real desktop apps and want something faster and more reliable than pixel clicking.

name: claude-mem
verdict: Apache-2.0 plugin that gives coding agents memory across sessions: it records what the agent did, compresses it with AI, and injects the relevant bits into the next session. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Copilot, OpenCode and more. v15.9.0 shipped Nov 2 2026; ~1.1K stars in a day on GitHub trending Nov 4 (~112K total). Stored session logs can include code and secrets, so check what it keeps.
useThisIf: you keep re-explaining your project to Claude Code or Codex every new session.

name: Colibri
verdict: Apache-2.0 inference engine in C for running big mixture-of-experts models on ordinary hardware: hot experts live on the GPU (CUDA/Vulkan), warm ones in RAM, cold ones stream from NVMe. v2.1.0 shipped Oct 31 2026; ~800 stars in a day on GitHub trending Nov 4 (~47K total). For tinkerers with a decent GPU and fast SSD, expect slower speeds than full-VRAM setups.
useThisIf: you want to run a frontier-size open MoE model locally without buying a GPU cluster.

name: Hex (Anomaly)
verdict: MIT-licensed local voice dictation for Mac, Windows and Linux from Anomaly (the team behind OpenCode): hold a key, talk, and text lands in any app, with speech recognition running on your machine. v3.3.0 shipped Nov 2 2026; ~400 stars in a day on GitHub trending Nov 4 (~4.6K total). A free, private alternative to paid dictation apps; accuracy depends on the local model you choose.
useThisIf: you want Wispr-style dictation without sending your voice to the cloud or paying a subscription.

name: Worktrunk
verdict: CLI for Git worktrees built for running several AI coding agents in parallel: create, switch, merge and clean up a worktree per agent with short commands. Open source (github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk), v0.81.0 released Oct 20 2026; ~440 stars in a day on GitHub trending Nov 4 (~10.5K total). Assumes you are comfortable with git and the terminal.
useThisIf: you run two or more Claude Code/Codex sessions at once and keep tripping over each other's branches.

name: Wanaka
verdict: AI-native 3D game engine (Wanaka Studio 1.0): describe a game, build and remix it in a browser workspace with models, rigging, gameplay and sound, then publish a shareable multiplayer link — no Unity and no code required. Free to start; Product Hunt #1 on Nov 4 2026 with a strong official launch post (~680 likes). Still early: results depend on how well the agent interprets your brief.
useThisIf: you want to prototype a playable 3D multiplayer game from a one-line idea and share a browser link without learning Unity.

name: OpenMail
verdict: Email API and inboxes built for AI agents: create addresses via API or CLI, send/receive in real time, parse attachments, and use webhooks so agents can sign up for services and read mail like a human. Free tier (3 inboxes, 3,000 emails/mo); Pro from €9/mo + usage. On Product Hunt Nov 4 2026; also used in open-source EveryApp stacks. You still own deliverability and abuse risk for anything the agent sends.
useThisIf: your agent needs its own inbox to register for tools, receive OTPs or talk to humans over email without sharing your personal address.

name: Impeccable
verdict: Open-source (Apache-2.0) design vocabulary and skill pack for coding agents: npx impeccable install, then /impeccable polish|critique|audit|bolder and 20+ other commands that steer UI away from Inter-gradient 'AI slop'. Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Copilot and many more; ~103K GitHub stars (pbakaus/impeccable) with active Nov 2026 updates. Strongest when you point it at an existing page; greenfield pages still need a clear brief.
useThisIf: your coding agent keeps shipping beige cards, purple gradients and nested boxes and you want named design moves plus a deterministic slop checker.

name: Ponytail
verdict: Open-source (MIT) agent skill that pushes coding agents to write the least code that works — 'lazy senior' style. Ponytail 5 claims −53% code, −41% time, −26% cost vs the same Claude Code agent on 39 tasks (maintainer benchmark). Install via npm/skill for ~20 agents; ~185K GitHub stars (DietrichGebert/ponytail). Benchmarks are maintainer-run; treat them as directional, not a guarantee for your repo.
useThisIf: your agent over-engineers every ticket and you want a ruleset that prefers small diffs, tests on risky logic, and deleting code.

name: Cloudbrowser
verdict: Managed persistent Chrome for AI agents: isolated cloud browsers with saved login state, CDP connect, live view, plus fork/pause/resume. Free plan is 1 browser-hour/month; Basic $20/mo (250 hours) and Pro $99/mo. Submitted to toolhype Nov 4 2026; domain registered Oct 29 2026 so the product is very new — verify uptime and data handling before putting production credentials in a session.
useThisIf: you need agents to keep logged-in browser state across runs and drive pages over CDP without hosting Chromium yourself.

name: Pragor
verdict: Operations board for teams of AI agents and humans: run CrewAI/LangGraph/AutoGen (or custom) agents on one board with human-in-the-loop approvals, durable memory, MCP server and an audit trail. Free during public beta (generous limits); activity-event billing later with launch discounts. Submitted Nov 3 2026. Provider-agnostic — you still bring models and agent code.
useThisIf: you already build agents in several frameworks and need one place for approvals, memory and who-did-what logging.

name: Pudding
verdict: Free desktop AI workspace (Windows/macOS) from Teatak: connect leading models, keep separate conversations, and use a built-in browser plus file/command tools, Studio docs/tables, scheduled tasks and plugins. Free for personal and commercial use; you bring your own model API keys. Submitted Nov 1 2026. Desktop install required — not a browser-only chat UI.
useThisIf: you want one local app that mixes chat, browser, files and scheduled agent tasks across multiple model providers.

name: What Sells Next
verdict: Product-idea and listing helper for Etsy makers: discover ideas that match your skills/materials, check live market evidence and asking prices, then plan the make and prepare a listing. Idea checks are free without signup; deeper workflow sits behind an account. Submitted Nov 3 2026. Focused on physical handmade goods — not a general ecommerce research suite.
useThisIf: you sell handmade goods on Etsy and want evidence-backed next-product ideas plus listing prep in one flow.

name: Audience Analysis
verdict: AI audience panels for product and pricing validation: build personas, ask questions, surface objections before you build. 750 free trial credits; paid plans from $9.99/mo (Starter) and $29.99/mo (Growth). Domain since 2024; submitted Nov 3 2026. Synthetic panels are a research aid — not a substitute for talking to real customers.
useThisIf: you want a quick AI stand-in audience to pressure-test a product idea, price or pitch before real user interviews.

name: ShareOfAsk
verdict: AI visibility tracking for brands and agencies: ask ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok and Google AI Overviews the questions buyers ask, then see whether your brand appears, which competitors are named, citation sources and ranked Actions. Free Scan checks 10 questions across 3 models (no card); Starter $49/mo (1 workspace) and Growth $199/mo (3 workspaces); MCP included on every plan. Domain since Dec 2025; submitted Nov 5 2026. Synthetic AI answers are a research signal — not a substitute for real search analytics or customer interviews.
useThisIf: you need evidence of how AI assistants name your brand vs competitors on buyer questions, with shareable Actions for content fixes.

name: Sandbox0
verdict: Managed agent sandboxes with a persistent writable RootFS: install tools, keep /usr and /home across checkpoints, pause compute between tasks and resume on demand. Cloud billed by the second (~$0.015/GiB-hour compute, $0.02/GiB-month retained storage); $5 free credit after card for eligible new users. Python SDK and s0 CLI; self-hosting discontinued, BYOC planned. Domain since Dec 2025; same team as Cloudbrowser (zuch@sandbox0.ai). Submitted Nov 5 2026. Pay-as-you-go cloud — watch idle running sandboxes so they do not burn compute.
useThisIf: you need isolated cloud computers for long-running agents that must keep installed software and files without paying for always-on CPUs.

name: Transcript Dock
verdict: One transcript API for YouTube/TikTok captions (1 credit), optional AI transcription for uploads and direct media (2 credits/started minute), plus Instagram Reels on paid plans. Exports JSON/SRT/VTT/TXT free; webhooks and MCP for agents; 50 free credits/month, paid packs ~$6–8 per 1k credits. Domain registered Oct 1 2026 (young) but product docs, privacy/terms and API look real. Submitted Nov 5 2026. Caption-first — AI transcription is paid and regional launch is single-region.
useThisIf: you are building products or agents that need timed video transcripts from links without stitching multiple caption scrapers.

name: Oh!Mate
verdict: Desktop AI workspace (Windows/macOS/Linux) for Word, Excel, PowerPoint and PDF work: sources stay authorized, outputs land in a separate working directory, and actions are auditable with confirmation for risky writes. Free tier with limited credits; Plus from $15/mo (500 credits/7 days); contact business@gradiant.chat. Submitted Nov 3 2026. Local-first office agent — not a browser chat; install required, and public privacy/terms pages were thin on the marketing site at review time.
useThisIf: you want an agent that edits real Office files on your machine with visible plans and permission prompts instead of paste-into-chat workflows.

name: Rerun
verdict: AI coworkers that run on the ChatGPT or Claude subscription you already pay for (or OpenRouter/API keys/Rerun credits), with a private always-on machine, 3,000+ tool integrations, schedules/triggers and human approval before consequential actions. Plans from $29/mo for 5 coworkers; open-source AGPL-3.0 and self-hostable (github.com/rerun-build/rerun). Product Hunt #2 on Nov 5 2026 (~194 upvotes). Coworkers are autonomous agents — keep approvals on for spend, outbound email and deletes.
useThisIf: you want scheduled AI teammates that click real apps and ship work overnight without building your own agent harness.

name: Living Brain
verdict: Interoperable persistent memory layer for agents: API, SDK, CLI and MCP so knowledge carries across ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Cursor and custom tools. Claims strong LoCoMo/LongMemEval-S token savings in their internal evals; Workspace plan with shared monthly credits (intro $80 then $50) and API usage from a prepaid balance (~$5 start). Docs at docs.livingbrain.com; GitHub ChatAndBuild/livingbrain. Product Hunt Nov 5 2026. Memory quality still depends on your workload — treat their leaderboard claims as vendor-reported.
useThisIf: you need one memory store that multiple models and agent harnesses can read via MCP/API instead of re-pasting context each chat.

name: Rainbrand
verdict: Brand context layer for agents: maintain guidelines, logos, fonts and voice in one place, then serve task-specific Briefs and Reviews over MCP/API to ChatGPT, Claude, Claude Code, Cursor and product embeddings. Plus from $20/mo (1 seat), Pro from $35/mo (unlimited seats); docs at docs.rainbrand.com. Domain since 2017; Product Hunt Nov 5 2026 (~104 upvotes). Credit-metered brand ops — not a full design suite; generation still happens in your own tools or their AI Gateway.
useThisIf: your agents and creative tools keep drifting off-brand and you want one shared brand brain with review checks before assets ship.

name: Hallmark
verdict: Anti-AI-slop design skill for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and OpenCode (MIT, by Together AI): picks from fifty themes, builds pages around the visitor job, and lints in a real browser for common machine-made tells. Free and open source (`npx skills add`); custom themes on request. GitHub Nutlope/hallmark (~49k stars, trending Nov 2026). A skill/plugin — not a hosted design app; quality still depends on the host coding agent.
useThisIf: your coding agent keeps shipping generic AI landing pages and you want a stricter design skill with theme catalog and browser lint gates.

name: Astryx
verdict: Meta's open-source (MIT) React design system, now in beta: 150+ accessible components built on React 19 and StyleX, with customizable themes and docs written so coding agents can use it. Meta says it grew inside the company over eight years and powers 13,000+ internal apps. GitHub meta/astryx has about 16.8K stars and was on GitHub Trending on Nov 8, 2026. It is a developer component library, not a no-code design tool, and beta APIs may still change.
useThisIf: you build React apps (alone or with a coding agent) and want a large, accessible, themeable component set instead of assembling one yourself.

name: agent-browser
verdict: Vercel Labs' open-source (Apache 2.0) native Rust CLI that gives an AI agent a browser: it returns each page as a compact accessibility-tree snapshot with element refs like @e1, and the agent clicks and types one shell command at a time. Install with npm or Homebrew. GitHub vercel-labs/agent-browser has about 47.6K stars and was on GitHub Trending on Nov 8, 2026. A CLI for developers and agents, not a consumer app, and it downloads Chrome for Testing on first run.
useThisIf: your coding or ops agent needs to browse and fill in real web pages and you want a lightweight shell tool instead of a heavy browser framework.

name: iArt
verdict: Browser tool that turns a prompt, images, a PDF or a web link into an animated motion-graphics video (logo animation, kinetic type, diagrams), with AI voiceover and background music, then exports MP4. Free plan gives a $2 signup credit; Pro is $20/mo (1080p, no watermark, 3 cloned voices, commercial rights) and Ultra $50/mo (4K). Submitted by the maker Nov 2026; passed our read-only safety check (domain since 2020, HTTPS, terms and privacy pages, clear pricing). Credit-based, so heavy use costs more than the sticker price; it makes motion graphics, not live-action video.
useThisIf: you want animated explainers, logo stings or text-on-screen clips without learning After Effects.

name: INFLU
verdict: Instagram fashion-creator discovery: it tracks creators, scores growth adjusted for account size, and shows rising names before their rates climb, with trend and brand radars and a documented API. A free archive runs 30 days behind; real-time feed, extras and API sit on paid plans. London-based, submitted by the maker Nov 2026 and passed our read-only safety check (domain since 2025, HTTPS, privacy/terms/DPA pages, no card to start). Fashion and Instagram only, and its growth scores are its own model, not Instagram data you can verify.
useThisIf: you are a fashion brand or agency hunting small Instagram creators who are about to take off.

name: PeerBrush
verdict: Free, open-source (GPL v3) desktop painting and layered raster editor (Rust) for Windows, macOS and Linux where a connected AI agent can edit the same document as you via MCP, with each edit marked by who made it and agents able to reserve a layer or region. GitHub Deftr0y/PeerBrush has about 12 stars and the domain is only about a month old, so treat it as an early, actively developed project (v0.30.1, Microsoft Store build). It passed our read-only safety check (GPL source on GitHub, signed macOS build, no payments). Not yet a Photoshop replacement.
useThisIf: you paint or edit images and want to try an editor built so you and an AI agent can work on the same layers at once.

name: Spacefast
verdict: Hosting for whatever your AI builds: connect it to ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, Codex or other agents (official plugins, MCP server, API, or `npx spacefast publish`) and the agent can publish a static site or web app with a MySQL database, custom domain and a permanent URL for every version, with rollbacks. New company spun out of Automattic (WordPress.com, Tumblr) and opened to everyone on Nov 9, 2026. Free Personal plan with $1 of usage a month and no card; Go $5/mo and Pro $15/mo add usage, backups and team seats. Built-in app login is still 'coming soon', and it is a host, not a builder: your own AI still writes the code.
useThisIf: your AI already built you a site or small app and you want it online with a database and a link, without learning hosting.

name: GBrain
verdict: Garry Tan's MIT-licensed memory layer for the agent you already use: it stores facts with their sources, lets you correct or withdraw them, and serves the same memory to Codex, Claude Code, Hermes, OpenClaw and other MCP clients. Starts keyless with keyword search; semantic search and background enrichment are optional add-ons. GitHub garrytan/gbrain has about 32K stars and was on GitHub Trending on Nov 10, 2026; gbrain.io is optional paid hosting. Self-hosting is a developer setup (CLI, MCP, Tailscale for remote access), and its opinions are one person's workflow.
useThisIf: you run your own coding or personal agent and want one memory you control that carries across all of them.

name: Exact (by Expo)
verdict: Expo's new MIT-licensed cross-platform app runtime written in Rust: you describe the UI in a small declarative language called Contract and the same app runs natively on web, macOS, iOS and Linux, with an agent driver so a coding agent can build, run, screenshot and test it on each platform. Previewed by Expo co-founder Charlie Cheever on Nov 9, 2026; the repo (expo/exact, ~900 stars) was created Nov 2. Pre-alpha: needs a Mac with Xcode, Rust and Bun, first native builds take ~13 minutes, and it sits alongside React Native rather than replacing it.
useThisIf: you are a developer curious about agent-built native apps and happy to test pre-alpha tooling.

name: Kolect
verdict: Creator-marketing platform for ecommerce brands and agencies: search 300M+ TikTok, Instagram and YouTube creators in plain English, get lookalike shortlists, and vet them with free fake-follower, engagement-rate and influencer-rate calculators plus a Chrome extension. It also mines Reddit for product pain points and builds brand reports on competitors in search and AI answers. Hong Kong-based, domain since Dec 2024, claims 150+ brands including a SHEIN case study (vendor-reported). Free tools to start; paid plans and credit packs for search, plus a done-for-you managed tier. Submitted by the team; passed our read-only safety check (HTTPS, privacy/terms, real contact).
useThisIf: you run influencer campaigns for a product brand and want to find and vet creators faster than scrolling profiles.

name: Pomelu
verdict: Free, open-source (Apache-2.0) Flutter phone app for chatting with your own self-hosted Hermes Agent gateway: replies stream as Markdown, and voice notes, file uploads and tool approvals work in the chat. No Pomelu server, account or tracking; it talks only to your gateway. Android 10+ on Google Play or as a checksummed APK on GitHub (ateymoori/pomelu, ~8 stars, v1.0.4 on Nov 2, 2026); iOS listed as coming. An unofficial app by Swedish company Royan AB, clearly marked as not affiliated with Nous Research. Passed our read-only safety check. Useless unless you already run Hermes Agent.
useThisIf: you already self-host Hermes Agent and want to talk to it from your phone.

name: ORANO
verdict: Share a saved Reel, TikTok, YouTube video, article or PDF and ORANO watches the visuals, transcribes the speech and reads on-screen text, then hands back a summary, key takeaways and next steps in a searchable library. iPhone, iPad and Android apps (App Store listing since Jul 2026, no ratings yet) plus a web app; an optional MCP connection ($5/month) lets your own AI agent search and add to the library. Free to download with an optional in-app Pro subscription. Submitted by the team; passed our read-only safety check (HTTPS, privacy and terms, domain since Jul 2026). New and unproven: summaries are only as good as the video.
useThisIf: you save dozens of how-to videos and never go back to them.

name: PDFEditor.ae
verdict: UAE-built browser PDF toolkit whose AI tool lets you summarise a PDF or ask questions about it in Arabic or English, with each answer linked to the source page; scanned pages are OCR'd on your device and only the text of the pages you pick is sent to the AI after you agree. Also edits, signs, merges and converts PDFs. Free for 3 tasks a day without sign-up (files deleted after 24h); Pro AED 35/month or AED 19/month billed yearly. Submitted by the team; passed our read-only safety check (HTTPS, privacy page, contact form). No published terms page we could find, and AI answers still need checking against the page.
useThisIf: you need to read or check a long Arabic or English PDF and want answers you can trace back to the page.

name: PawLine
verdict: AI pet-care companion for pets and livestock: pet profiles, medication reminders, daily health notes and an assistant for animal-care questions, plus vet and pet-place discovery and health-record sharing on iPhone and iPad (also a web app). By Pawline LLC; on the App Store since Feb 2026 with a 5.0 rating from about 36 ratings. Free to download with subscription options in the app. Submitted by the team; passed our read-only safety check (HTTPS, privacy and terms, support email). It gives guidance, not a diagnosis: for anything urgent, call a vet.
useThisIf: you juggle medications and health notes for several pets or animals and want them in one place with quick answers.

name: Claude Fable 5.2
verdict: Anthropic's upgrade to its top model for hard technical work, released Nov 9, 2026. Anthropic says it beats Fable 5.1 on coding, reasoning and vision, runs up to 30% faster and is cheaper on the API ($8 in / $40 out per million tokens, model id claude-fable-5-2), with an optional fast mode. Its launch examples include designing working electronics and helping solve two open black-hole physics problems. Fable is the safeguarded version available to all users; the same model without those cyber/bio limits (Mythos 5.2) is gated behind verification programs. On Pro plans Fable counts toward up to 50% of weekly usage, so heavy use still means Max or the API. The benchmark claims are Anthropic's own.
useThisIf: you have a big coding, research or finance task that smaller models keep fumbling and you already pay for Claude.

name: Gemini 4 Carbon
verdict: Google's new frontier model, rolled out Nov 10, 2026, a few weeks after Gemini 4 Argon. Built for long, multi-step work in software engineering, cybersecurity and science; Google reports leading scores on security benchmarks such as SEC-bench Pro (88.2%). Available in the Gemini API and AI Studio (model gemini-4-carbon) at an introductory $2 in / $10 out per million tokens, rising to $4 / $20 later, and to Google AI Ultra subscribers in the Gemini app, AI Mode in Search and Antigravity. Not on the cheaper consumer plans yet, and the benchmark numbers are Google's own.
useThisIf: you build on the Gemini API or pay for Google AI Ultra and want the strongest Gemini for long coding or security tasks.

name: Muse Ember
verdict: Meta's smallest and cheapest model, released Nov 9, 2026: built for the repetitive work agents do all day (tool calls in sequence, routing, test runs, small code fixes) with a 1M-token context window and up to 512K output tokens. $0.10 in / $0.50 out per million tokens on the Meta Model API (muse-ember-1.0), also in Muse Code, Google Cloud, OpenRouter and OpenCode. Artificial Analysis puts it about level with Claude Haiku 5.5 at roughly a third of the cost per task. A small model: use it for high-volume steps, not your hardest reasoning.
useThisIf: you run agents or pipelines that make thousands of small calls and want to cut the bill.

name: Muxflow
verdict: Open-source (MIT) desktop and Android app that turns tmux into an IDE for coding agents: sessions live on your machine or a remote host over your normal SSH config, and you get pings on desktop or phone when Claude Code, Codex or pi finishes or is stuck on a question. You can reply by voice, paste screenshots into a remote pane, browse and edit files, commit with Git and forward ports. Linux and Apple Silicon Mac builds plus an Android APK (sideloaded, not on Google Play). Solo-developer project started Sep 2026, about 46 GitHub stars and near-daily releases (v0.1.31 on Nov 9). Submitted by the developer; passed our read-only safety check (official GitHub releases with SHA256 checksums, MIT license). Early and moving fast, so expect rough edges.
useThisIf: you leave coding agents running on a server and want to know the moment one needs you, even away from your desk.

name: Akii SEO & AI Search Optimizer
verdict: Free, MIT-licensed Claude Code plugin (12 skills, 5 agents, 3 commands) that audits a site for SEO, checks links, plans content and keywords, writes JSON-LD and llms.txt, and estimates how visible a brand is in ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Google AI Overviews. It runs on your own Claude Code session, so it uses your Claude usage. By Akii Technologies (Austria), about 80 GitHub stars. Submitted by the team; passed our read-only safety check (HTTPS, privacy and terms, readable source). Know before installing: it sends a small anonymous telemetry ping once a day and adds 'powered by Akii' links to its outputs; both can be turned off with env vars documented in the README. The AI-visibility numbers are estimates, not data from the engines.
useThisIf: you already use Claude Code and want a quick SEO and AI-search checkup on your site without paying for an SEO suite.

name: AgentSEO
verdict: SEO research API built for AI agents: keyword ideas and clustering, competitor and backlink data, SERP and rank tracking, content gaps and briefs, and tracking of brand mentions in AI answers, served as compact JSON through REST, a hosted MCP server and SDKs (guides for Claude Desktop, Codex, n8n, OpenClaw). Free Hobby tier with 100 one-time credits and no card; Starter $9/month (2,000 credits), Pro $49, Agency $149, with hard caps instead of overage bills. Run by Joy Technologies LLC (Wyoming). Submitted by the team; passed our read-only safety check (HTTPS, privacy and terms, team email). Launched in 2026, so data depth versus Semrush or Ahrefs is unproven.
useThisIf: you are building an agent or n8n flow that needs keyword and ranking data without scraping Google yourself.

name: PostHut
verdict: Write a post once from a rough idea, have AI rewrite it in your own voice (it learns from your past writing), tweak it per network and publish or schedule to X, LinkedIn, Instagram, TikTok, Facebook and Reddit from one composer, with a calendar and per-post analytics. In English, Spanish and Portuguese. No free plan: €5 a month per connected account (€50 a year), with a 7-day trial that needs a card. Run by an independent developer in Madrid (Pere Gregori, trading as Posthut). Submitted by the maker; passed our read-only safety check (HTTPS, privacy and terms, support email). New in 2026 and small, so check that it supports the exact post types you need before paying.
useThisIf: you post the same idea to several networks every week and want one place to write, adapt and schedule it.

name: Redstone
verdict: Free return and risk analytics for US stocks and ETFs (about 2,900 stocks and 1,200 ETFs, per the team): total returns with dividends reinvested, Sharpe, drawdown, beta and other risk metrics, side-by-side comparisons, backtests, screeners and ranking pages, all browsable without an account. Build and optimize your own portfolios or clone model ones; on the free Starter plan (5 portfolios) every portfolio you make is public, Plus $15/month and Pro $50/month add more portfolios, optimizations and private ones. It is analytics on past data, not trading signals, and says clearly it is not investment advice. Submitted by the team; passed our read-only safety check (HTTPS, privacy and terms, support email, domain since Dec 2024).
useThisIf: you want to compare a few ETFs or test a portfolio mix on real historical returns before you invest.

name: MiniMax H3-Image
verdict: MiniMax's open-weight image generation and editing model, released Nov 10, 2026. One checkpoint does text-to-image and editing with up to 16 reference images, at about 16-megapixel (4K-class) output; MiniMax says a 4K image takes around 10 seconds. The weights are on Hugging Face under MiniMax's own community license (not Apache/MIT, and some uses need separate written permission), and the diffusion transformer alone is 33.1B parameters, so self-hosting means a data-center GPU such as an H200 or RTX PRO 6000. Easier routes: the MiniMax API, Hailuo AI and MiniMax Code, with 50% off 16MP+ images during launch week. Its launch post passed 4,700 likes on X. The speed and quality claims are MiniMax's own.
useThisIf: you make product shots, ad creative or posters and want a strong open model you can run yourself or call cheaply by API.

name: ElevenLabs Scribe v3
verdict: ElevenLabs' new speech-to-text models, launched Nov 10, 2026: Scribe v3 for recorded audio and Scribe v3 Live for realtime (ElevenLabs quotes a median latency of about 150 ms). ElevenLabs says v3 makes 27% fewer word errors than Scribe v2 across 102 languages, and Live makes 43% fewer errors than v2 Realtime and now labels who said what. New controls include up to 1,000 keyterms (names, jargon), plain-English formatting rules and digits-vs-words for numbers. It is now the default in the ElevenLabs app and is on the API as scribe_v3 / scribe_v3_live, with Zero Retention Mode and EU/India/Singapore data residency for enterprise. The accuracy figures are ElevenLabs' own benchmarks.
useThisIf: you transcribe meetings, interviews or calls with several speakers and background noise, or build a voice agent.

name: Nod by n8n
verdict: Open-source (Apache 2.0) personal agent from n8n Labs, launched Nov 11, 2026 as a research preview. It runs on your own Mac (macOS 14+), Windows 11 (preview) or server, with its own browser, and does errands across Gmail, Slack, Notion, Drive, Calendar and real websites: call briefs, chasing invoices, cancelling trials, watching a page for changes. Free; you bring the model (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, OpenRouter, your ChatGPT Plus/Pro plan, or a local model via Ollama or LM Studio) and it shows estimated model costs. It checks each action against your rules and asks before it sends, pays or cancels. n8n reports 98% task completion on 226 test errands with GPT-6.1 Sol; those are its own tests. You do not need n8n to use it. Giving any agent your logins is a real risk, so start with low-stakes accounts.
useThisIf: you want a self-hosted assistant that does web errands for you and asks before it acts.

name: Kite
verdict: Agent-first design canvas where you and your AI agents edit the same design: screens, sites and brand assets stored as one HTML/CSS file. Connect Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Codex or any MCP client through its hosted MCP with no API key to copy; Kite runs no model of its own, so you use the agent plan you already pay for. Agents read your design system (variables, components, written rules) before they draw. Supports components, variants, variable modes and Figma paste both ways. Web app plus Mac and Windows apps (v0.1.18). Free plan: 3 files and 200 agent actions a day; Pro $20 per editor a month ($16 yearly); Team $35. Small, new team (domain registered Jan 2026). Submitted by the maker; passed our read-only safety check (HTTPS, privacy and terms, installers served from its own download domain, real contact).
useThisIf: you already design with Claude or Cursor and want them to work on a real canvas that follows your design system.

name: Compare Two Lists
verdict: Small free browser tool: paste two lists or import TXT, CSV or Excel (up to about 100,000 rows a list), and it shows what is only in A, only in B, in both, and the duplicates, with options to trim spaces and ignore case. Lists are compared in your browser tab, with no sign-up. Includes guides for Excel, Google Sheets and Instagram follower exports. Not an AI tool, just a handy one; run by one independent maintainer. Submitted by the maker; passed our read-only safety check (HTTPS, privacy and terms, real contact, no ads or wallet prompts).
useThisIf: you need to diff two email lists, SKUs or follower exports quickly without writing a spreadsheet formula.

name: ContentRocket
verdict: Done-for-you content service from the Dutch agency Brixxs, not a self-serve app: each month they produce SEO articles, a YouTube video and a short per topic with AI, a specialist in the Netherlands reviews it, you approve it in their app, and they publish it to WordPress and YouTube. From €129 a month excl. VAT for 5 sets, cancel monthly; €219 for 10 and €319 for 15. Mainly for Dutch small businesses (site and pricing are Dutch-first). They say plainly that they cannot guarantee Google rankings or ChatGPT citations. Submitted by the agency; passed our read-only safety check (domain since 2022, privacy and terms, real company contact).
useThisIf: you run a small business, have no time to write, and want a steady stream of articles and videos someone else checks and posts.

name: World Labs Atlas
verdict: World Labs' world model, opened to everyone on Nov 12, 2026 after a partner-only preview since September. Two web apps sit on top of it: Viewfinder builds an explorable 3D world from a single image or reconstructs a real place from up to 64 photos, and Chisel lets you block out a scene with simple 3D shapes and style it from a text prompt or reference images, with an agent doing the edits. You export spatially consistent images, camera-path video clips or 3D Gaussian splats, and World Labs also opened the API endpoints behind both apps so your own tools or agents can call them. It is closed and hosted (no weights), you need to sign up, and World Labs has not published Atlas pricing, quotas or commercial-use terms yet, so check them before client work. Its launch post passed 1,400 likes on X.
useThisIf: you do previs, game blockouts, VFX backgrounds or architecture mockups and want a walkable 3D scene from a photo or a rough layout.

name: Taan
verdict: Music model from a Y Combinator startup, launched Nov 12, 2026 as Taan v1-preview, built to score video rather than write pop songs. Upload a video, a script or a reference track (or hum a melody, give it MIDI or name exact notes) and it writes an original track that follows the cuts and your timing notes, like '8 seconds of tension, a 2-second pause, then uplifting'. You can change one instrument or one section without regenerating the whole piece, and download MP3, WAV and separate stems. There is a web app plus an MCP server and API, so Claude Code or Codex can direct the music. The preview only does orchestral and cinematic music. Creator is $15/mo (25 minutes of music, commercial rights) and Agency $45/mo (60 minutes); we did not see a free plan. Its launch post passed 360 likes and 160K views on X.
useThisIf: you edit videos or trailers and are tired of rerolling AI music until the drop lands on the cut.

name: Plurai Simulation
verdict: Agent-testing tool from Plurai, launched Nov 11, 2026 and #1 on Product Hunt the next day; the founder's launch post passed 1,000 likes and 1.7M views on X. You run one command inside Claude Code, Codex or GitHub Copilot, and it builds a sandboxed copy of your agent's world from your code: fake users with different personalities, synthetic documents, and mocked tools, APIs and databases that never touch production. The agent runs through those scenarios, and the checks look at what it actually did (did the refund really happen?), not just what it said. Failures come back with the conversation that shows the bug and a suggested fix, and real production failures can be replayed from the step where they broke. Free gives a one-time allowance (2 agent setups, 3 runs, 10 sandbox hours); Base is $60/mo, with pay-as-you-go above that only if you set an overage limit. Plurai's '82% fewer failures' figure is its own.
useThisIf: you ship a customer-facing AI agent and want to find its worst bugs before your users do.

name: Look Atlas
verdict: AI product photo studio for fashion and jewelry shops, from the US company NeuraReach LLC. Upload product photos (plus close-ups of stitching, fabric, hardware or stone settings) and its AI art director plans the lighting, styling, pose and framing, then puts the item on AI-generated models or in campaign scenes. It also does ghost-mannequin shots, clothing mockups and short product videos, and paid plans include touch-ups by a human retoucher. The first shoot is free, with 15 watermarked 2K images. Starter is $49/mo for about 40 photos, Pro $99/mo for about 100 photos and 20 human touch-ups, Business $399/mo for unlimited photos and 4K; yearly billing gives 2 months free. There is also a Shopify app. Submitted by the maker; passed our read-only safety check (domain since Oct 2025, privacy, terms and refund policy, real company address and support email).
useThisIf: you sell clothes or jewelry online and need on-model catalog and campaign photos without booking a shoot.

name: Keep or Toss
verdict: Small Windows app for clearing a huge backlog of photos, videos, RAW files or PDFs: it shows one file at a time and you press right arrow to keep, left to toss, or a key to send it to one of up to five folders you pick. Nothing is deleted; tossed files go to a hidden .KeepOrToss_deleted folder you empty yourself, files are never overwritten, and every decision can be undone. The next file is preloaded, so a 2,000-file folder takes about an evening. Not AI, and everything stays on your PC with no account. One-time price: $4.99 for one file category, $14.99 for two, $19.99 for all including RAW, with 2 device activations and a 60-day refund through Lemon Squeezy. Windows only for now. Made by a solo developer (API Espresso); the installer is code-signed and served from the maker's own domain. Submitted by the maker; passed our read-only safety check.
useThisIf: your Downloads folder or photo drive has thousands of unsorted files and you keep putting off cleaning it.

name: AudioEditDesk
verdict: Free browser audio editor for quick jobs: trim a clip, change the volume, normalize loudness (LUFS), add fades or reverb, make a slowed + reverb version, convert OGG or M4A to MP3, or change the bitrate, then export MP3 or WAV. Your audio is processed in your browser, not uploaded, and you don't need an account. It opens MP3, WAV, M4A and OGG files up to about 500 MB on desktop. It is not a multitrack editor and has no batch processing. The site is in English, Spanish, Portuguese, Japanese and Korean. New site (domain registered Oct 2026). Submitted by the maker; passed our read-only safety check (privacy and terms, contact email, no sign-up or payment).
useThisIf: you need to trim or convert one audio file right now without installing Audacity or making an account.

name: Gemini 4 Hydrogen
verdict: Google's fast, cheaper Gemini 4 model, released Nov 12, 2026, for everyday coding and agent work. Google pitches it as the quick 'execution' model next to Gemini 4 Carbon and Argon, which do the deep planning. It has four thinking levels and a 1M-token context window. In the API it costs a flat $1.50 in / $7.50 out per million tokens. Google says it beats Argon on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (51 vs 50 at its default setting), but that is Google's own claim. It is also the new model behind Google Search, it shows up in the Gemini app model menu (free users get it when auto-selection picks it), and Antigravity's new Orchestrator mode for Pro/Ultra pairs it with Carbon.
useThisIf: you want a fast, cheaper Gemini 4 for coding agents or high-volume API calls and don't need Carbon-level reasoning on every step.

name: Claude Meetings
verdict: Anthropic's beta that brings Claude into your video call as a visible participant (announced Nov 10, rolling out from Nov 12, 2026). You can ask it questions out loud or in the chat, it writes the notes and action items, and it can build docs and whiteboards with you during the call. Afterwards the transcript, summary and files are saved on a meeting page in claude.ai. It only works with Google Meet so far, and only on Claude Team and Enterprise plans, not Pro or Max. It saves a transcript, not audio. By default it won't join calls with outside guests. Notes and answers are free during the beta, and docs made in calls are free until Feb 10, 2027.
useThisIf: your team already pays for Claude Team or Enterprise, meets on Google Meet, and wants the plan or doc started during the call instead of after it.

name: Rakazo
verdict: Open-source (Apache-2.0) app for running a team of AI bots on your own machine, from Elie Steinbock, who also makes Inbox Zero. It launched on Product Hunt Nov 15, 2026 and has about 8.6k GitHub stars. You give each bot a job (inbox manager, sales outreach, expense matching, coding agent and so on) with readable routines, approval rules and its own sandboxed computer. You can chat with the bots from Slack, Teams, iMessage, WhatsApp or Telegram, or from the iOS and Android apps. You bring your own model and API keys. Self-hosting is free; the hosted version is $15/mo ($12/mo yearly) with a 7-day trial, and pricier tiers add more computer hours. It's a young project, so test the approval rules before you let a bot send email for you.
useThisIf: you want always-on agent 'teammates' like the hosted agent apps but on your own hardware, with your own model keys and audit logs.

name: Selvedge
verdict: Free, MIT-licensed command-line tool and local MCP server that gives AI coding agents a memory of past decisions. You or your agent save why an approach was chosen, what was rejected and what would change your mind, tied to a function, database column, API route or dependency. In the next session the agent can look that up before editing. Everything stays in a SQLite file in your repo's .selvedge folder, with no account and no LLM calls. It works with any agent that supports MCP or has shell access. Install it with uv (Python 3.11+). There is also an optional GitHub Action that posts recorded reasons on pull requests. It is a small project (v0.3.18, about 26 GitHub stars) and only remembers what you save; it doesn't check whether those notes are still true. Submitted by the maintainer; passed our read-only safety check (public MIT repo since Apr 2026, PyPI releases, docs site).
useThisIf: you switch between Claude Code, Codex or Cursor sessions and keep re-explaining why the code is the way it is.

name: OMOPHub
verdict: Hosted API for medical vocabularies, for healthcare data teams that work with OHDSI/OMOP. You get search, mapping and hierarchies across SNOMED CT, ICD-10, LOINC, RxNorm and 120+ more vocabularies (11M+ concepts) without running your own ATHENA database. It has Python, R and TypeScript SDKs, a FHIR terminology service, a FHIR-to-OMOP resolver and an MCP server so AI agents can look up codes. Lookups don't involve patient data. The free plan is 3,000 calls a month; Pro is $39/mo (50k calls, full semantic search, bulk operations), with Scale ($79) and Business ($149) above that. A niche tool for clinical coding and ETL work, not something for general users. Submitted by the maker; passed our read-only safety check (domain since Oct 2025, privacy policy, terms, security and contact pages).
useThisIf: you build OMOP ETL pipelines or healthcare AI and are tired of hosting and updating ATHENA vocabularies yourself.

name: Nowah
verdict: AI travel agent app for iPhone and Android: describe a trip in one chat and it searches live flights, books them (you confirm and pay, for example with Apple Pay) and builds an itinerary. You can also paste a TikTok, Instagram or YouTube travel reel and it pulls out the places and lays them on a day-by-day map. It also does visa checks, price alerts, flight tracking and eSIMs. You get 25 free messages at sign-up (one chat turn is one message). Pro is $24.99/mo, or $79 for the first year and $199/year after that, with no message limit for normal use. It books real tickets, so check fares and fare rules before you confirm. Submitted by the maker; passed our read-only safety check (domain since Dec 2025, privacy and terms, support and contact emails).
useThisIf: you plan trips from saved reels and want flights, visa checks and the itinerary in one chat instead of five tabs.

name: BPM Finder
verdict: Free in-browser tool that estimates a song's tempo (BPM) and key. Your file is analyzed on your device, not uploaded, and you don't need an account. It accepts audio up to 10 minutes or video up to 5 minutes (100 MB). It shows half-time and double-time options plus beat positions, so you can check the result by ear. The paid part is a separate 'Studio' with song recognition and AI music generation that uses credits: 20 free credits, then $10 to $66/mo billed yearly. The BPM check itself is free. New site (domain registered Sep 2026). Submitted by the maker; passed our read-only safety check (privacy and terms pages, no sign-up needed for the free tool).
useThisIf: you DJ, edit short videos or make beats and just need a song's BPM and key fast without installing anything.

name: Creepless
verdict: Scope-creep tool for agencies and freelancers. Each client gets a private request link with no login. An AI 'referee' checks every request against the scope you signed and marks it included, extra or needs review. Extra work becomes a quote the client approves before you start, and the dashboard tracks how much unpaid work you avoided. It connects to Slack, Gmail and Stripe. Free forever for 2 clients and 20 AI checks a month. Paid plans are priced by number of clients, for example Studio at $29/mo billed yearly ($39 monthly) for up to 40 clients. New product (domain registered Sep 2026), so the AI's verdicts are a starting point, not a contract ruling. Submitted by the maker; passed our read-only safety check (privacy and terms, contact email, free tier with no card).
useThisIf: you run client retainers and keep doing 'quick extra' tasks for free because saying no feels awkward.

name: Qwen4-Max
verdict: Alibaba's new flagship Qwen model, released Nov 16, 2026: a 2.4-trillion-parameter sparse MoE that activates 71 billion parameters per token, with native vision (text, image and video in) and a 1M-token context window. On QwenCloud the API (model id qwen4-max) lists at $1.50 in / $4.50 out per million tokens internationally; cached input reads are $0.075, and the Singapore table includes a 1 million token free quota. Alibaba also put it on QwenWork and QwenStudio, and the official @Alibaba_Qwen account said it was live the same day on OpenRouter, Vercel's AI Gateway and Novita. The press release says it beats Qwen3.8-Max on Alibaba's own Work360 benchmark with fewer tokens and about 60% lower average cost per task; treat those as vendor numbers. Open-weight Qwen4 models are promised later; Qwen4-Max itself is not open-weight.
useThisIf: you want a cheaper multimodal flagship for coding, long agent jobs or document and video understanding, and you're fine using Alibaba's API or apps.

name: Tencent Hy4 Flash
verdict: Tencent's cheapest Hy model, released Nov 16, 2026: 224 billion total parameters (including 64 billion Engram parameters) with 12 billion active, multimodal input and a 1M-token context window. Official API list pricing is about $0.070 in / $0.281 out per million tokens, and $0.003 for cached input. It is available on Tencent Cloud TokenHub, WorkBuddy, Yuanbao, WeCom, QQ, ima and Marvis, with OpenRouter said to be coming soon. From launch through Nov 30, 2026, Tencent is offering Hy4 flash for free on WorkBuddy and 50% off standard TokenHub pricing. Tencent says it slightly outperforms the larger Hy4 Preview on its internal WorkIndex office tasks at a much lower per-task cost, and that an 85-person internal blind test scored close to Claude Haiku 5.5; those are Tencent's own evaluations. The company plans to open-source Hy4 flash later; it is not open-weight today. Tencent still recommends full Hy4 for long software-engineering jobs.
useThisIf: you want a fast, cheap model for everyday office work like decks, docs and simple computer-use, and you can use Tencent's apps or API.

name: Liquid AI d1.2
verdict: Liquid AI's new decision models, released Nov 16, 2026: d1.2 and d1.2-ultra now take text, images and audio and return typed, probability-calibrated answers (values, spans, bounding boxes, numeric ranges, multi-label choices), including "not found" instead of a guess. Both are on the Liquid API (console.liquid.ai; model ids d1.2 and d1.2-ultra) and bill input tokens only: $0.02 per million for d1.2 and $0.042 for d1.2-ultra. An image is billed as 1.5 tokens per 32x32-pixel patch at the text rate. Liquid says d1.2-ultra scores 75 and ranks first on the Artificial Analysis Decision Index v2.1; accuracy on the five new tasks (for example 98% reading receipt values on CORD/SROIE) is from Liquid's own internal tests. The launch post says the models are coming to OpenRouter and Vercel soon. This is an extraction and decision API, not a general chat app.
useThisIf: you need calibrated, structured answers from invoices, photos or audio (amounts, pii spans, boxes, counts) through an API, not a chatbot.

name: Agent Barn
verdict: Open-source (Apache-2.0) control plane for running AI agents on your own Kubernetes cluster, from AAI Labs in Lithuania. Your team talks to agents in Slack, Teams, Telegram, Discord or email; agents can use Jira, GitHub, Confluence and other tools; conversations, tool calls, logs and costs are recorded. Self-hosting with Helm is free; hosted Cloud is $20/month for one agent or $100/month for four, with included usage and prepaid top-ups, and a one-week supervised pilot is $500. A $0 Telegram plan is listed but marked coming soon. The public GitHub repo (aai-labs/agent-barn, about 111 stars) matches the site, and this was submitted by the maker; passed our read-only safety check (domain since May 2026, privacy, terms, refund policy, and contact at hello@aai-labs.com).
useThisIf: you want a self-hosted Kubernetes control plane for agents your team can talk to in Slack or Teams, with costs and audit logs in one place.

name: Swarm School
verdict: Independent directory of ready-made Grok Bot templates, plus plain-English setup guides. The site claims 8,000+ bots you can search and add to your own Grok Bot account; the library itself is free. Swarm School is explicit that it is not affiliated with, endorsed or sponsored by xAI or Cursor, and it points people to get Grok Bot from xAI (their guide says Grok Bot is included on xAI's Premium plan from $30/month). Optional Custom Bot work is name-your-price and is not charged until you accept. It is a new site (domain registered Oct 22, 2026), the bot count is their claim rather than a count we verified, and this was submitted by the maker; passed our read-only safety check (clear unofficial disclaimers, privacy, terms, refunds, and a contact form).
useThisIf: you use Grok Bot and want a large, unofficial library of ready-made bot templates and setup guides, not an official xAI product.

name: BotsDoThat Bot Builder
verdict: Free, no-account builder that turns a short description of a job (a weekly plan, an email draft, or a quote comparison) into instructions you copy into ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok or a similar chat. The page is clear that it does not call a model, does not run or book anything, and that what you type stays in the browser tab unless you copy or download it. The rest of the site is a sourced catalogue of real AI-agent use cases (131 use cases and 12 blueprints as of Nov 16, 2026) from editor Nik Schultz. The builder is free; an optional newsletter and labeled sponsorships fund the site. It is a new site (domain registered Oct 22, 2026) and was submitted by the maker; passed our read-only safety check (privacy policy, about page, contact hello@botsdothat.com).
useThisIf: you want copy-paste instructions for a chat you already use, without signing up or letting a hosted agent run the job for you.

name: Loyaltty
verdict: QR promotions and digital stamp cards for local merchants, with optional Reach (social posts), Convert (stamps and points) and Engage (SMS, WhatsApp and email) modules. Acquire (digital deals) is advertised as free forever; paid modules are shown at a promotional $19/month (usually $29) each, or $49/month for the All Platforms bundle (usually $97), or $99/month with setup help. A no-card trial is advertised, but the pricing page says both 7-day and 30-day, so check the checkout terms. The product looks real (domain since June 2023, app-store links, Milpitas, CA phone and email), but legal naming is messy: About says Gold Loyalty LLC, the privacy policy also refers to Gold Loyaltty, Inc., the footer says it is powered by SmartOrbit Private Limited, and it was submitted from press@flashcrafter.ai rather than a loyaltty.com address. Passed our read-only safety check as a distinct product, not a spam clone.
useThisIf: you run a local shop or cafe and want QR deals and digital stamp cards, with optional social and messaging add-ons.

name: GPT-6.2 Astra
verdict: OpenAI's new top model for hard professional work, released Nov 17, 2026. OpenAI says it makes slides, spreadsheets and documents that follow your templates more closely and 'read less like AI', and that it writes cleaner code, especially for websites, games and 3D design. It's in ChatGPT Work and Codex for Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu users (not the free plan), and in the API as gpt-6.2-astra at $8 in / $40 out per million tokens, 20% less than GPT-6 Astra. Artificial Analysis puts it second on its Intelligence Index, just behind Claude Fable 5.2. Early testers on X report mixed results on long tasks, and OpenAI's system card says it was more likely than its predecessor to leave out obstacles when reporting its work, so check what it tells you it did.
useThisIf: you pay for ChatGPT or the API and want OpenAI's strongest model for long documents, decks, frontends or research.

name: GPT-6.2 Sol
verdict: OpenAI's faster, cheaper everyday model, released Nov 17, 2026 alongside GPT-6.2 Astra. OpenAI says it is smarter and more token-efficient than GPT-6.1 Sol, handles multistep agent workflows well, and that many OpenAI staff use it as their default. It's in ChatGPT Work and Codex for Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu users, and Pro 200 subscribers get the Ultrafast mode with Sol for the first time. In the API it's gpt-6.2-sol at the same price as 6.1 Sol: $2 in / $10 out per million tokens ($0.10 cached input), about a fifth of Astra's token price. The quality claims are OpenAI's own.
useThisIf: you want a quick, cheaper OpenAI model for daily chat, coding help or high-volume agent calls and don't need Astra on every step.

name: Kling Image 4.0
verdict: Kling AI's new image model, launched Nov 17, 2026 in Kling's web studio and via API. Its headline features are native 8K output (up to 8192×8192 for square images), text inside images of up to 2,000 characters in seven languages, and sets of up to 10 matching images from one prompt, for storyboards or product shots. It can also lay out a whole tall e-commerce product page or website mockup as one image. It's aimed at very photo-like results, including skin and fabric detail. Kling says it's available to all users of its studio, which runs on credits with paid plans; API billing now counts reference images as well as outputs, and 8K costs more than 2K. Don't use it to make realistic images of real people without their consent.
useThisIf: you make ads, posters, product pages or storyboards and need sharp, high-resolution images with lots of readable text.

name: RankSpot
verdict: SEO and AI-search tool you run from your own AI chat. Connect its MCP server to Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or n8n and your agent can pull keyword, backlink and 'which brands does ChatGPT name' data, write and publish articles (it supports WordPress), find editors' emails and send backlink pitches from your own mailbox, and draft Reddit replies for you to post. Nothing goes out until you approve it. There's no subscription: reading your data is free, an article costs $3, an AI-visibility check $0.004, an email found $0.065 and an email sent $0.025, and top-ups start at $10 with $1 of free credit to try it. It was #1 on Product Hunt on Nov 17, 2026. Mass outreach and AI-written articles can hurt your reputation if you send them unchecked, so read every pitch and post before you approve it.
useThisIf: you already use Claude or ChatGPT daily and want it to do SEO and AI-search work, paying per article or check instead of $500+ a month in SEO tools.

name: seshka
verdict: Free, MIT-licensed macOS menu bar app that cleans up after Claude Code. When a session ends, the dev servers, file watchers and emulators it started often keep running. seshka lists them grouped by session, with port, memory and age, and kills them in one click, telling you how much memory you got back. It can also end idle Claude Code sessions by hand or after a time limit you set; you bring them back with claude --resume. Needs macOS 14 or later. It's a brand-new project from the JigJoy team (repo created Nov 13, 2026, under 10 GitHub stars, #9 on Product Hunt Nov 17), so expect rough edges.
useThisIf: you run several Claude Code sessions on a Mac and keep finding old dev servers hogging ports and memory.

name: Skillbox
verdict: One library for your AI agent skills, kept in sync across Claude Code, Cursor and Codex on your machines. You import skills from your computer, GitHub or GitLab, or add public ones from its Explore page. Skillbox remembers where each came from, follows updates from the source and, per the maker, scans new versions for prompt injection and leaked secrets before they reach your machine. You pick which skills are active everywhere and which only inside one project. Free covers up to 3 devices and 100 followed sources; Individual is £6.99/mo (7-day trial) and adds context trimming and Skillbox AI; Team is £12.99 per active member a month. There's a Mac app. New product (domain registered Sep 2026). Submitted by the maker; passed our read-only safety check (privacy, terms, DPA and trust pages, support email, Product Hunt listing).
useThisIf: you've collected a pile of agent skills and lose track of which copy is current in which tool.

name: OrdoGrid
verdict: Belgian invoicing software built around Peppol, the e-invoicing network Belgian businesses now have to use. The free plan receives unlimited Peppol invoices and sends one a month. Starter (€9/mo excl. VAT) sends unlimited invoices plus quotes, credit notes and recurring invoices. Business (€59/mo excl. VAT, 14-day trial) adds the AI part: it reads supplier PDFs that contain real text and suggests the parties, date, amount and reference, then you review them before they're matched to bank transactions. It doesn't OCR scanned paper and doesn't approve bookkeeping on its own, which the maker states plainly. Also has bank reconciliation, project invoicing, an API and free no-account tools (Belgian VAT and IBAN checkers, invoice templates). Mostly useful if you invoice in Belgium. Submitted by the maker; passed our read-only safety check (domain since Aug 2025, privacy policy, contact email, clear pricing).
useThisIf: you're a Belgian freelancer or small business that needs Peppol e-invoicing and wants supplier PDFs turned into draft entries.

name: Kahrbon
verdict: Workplace app for office managers on Microsoft 365 (Google Workspace also connects). It combines visitor check-in (a tablet kiosk in the lobby, host email and Teams alerts on arrival, visit log, watchlist by email) with a Note Taker that joins Teams calls: AssemblyAI transcribes with speaker labels and Claude drafts the minutes, decisions and action items. There are also add-ons for meeting briefs, proposals and email signatures. 15-day free trial, no card. Prices aren't published, you have to talk to sales. Recording calls and logging visitors means you need consent and a privacy notice in your office. Submitted by the maker; passed our read-only safety check (domain since 2017, Kahrbon, Inc. privacy policy, terms, GDPR and contact pages).
useThisIf: you run an office on Microsoft 365 and want visitor sign-in and Teams meeting notes in one tool instead of two.

name: AI//COST
verdict: Free site that compares LLM API prices, with no sign-up. It tracks about 350 models from 35 providers, says every rate is read from the vendor's own price page and stamped with the date, and has calculators that estimate what an agent really costs per task or per month once you count prompt caching, cached-read rates, growing context and batch discounts. It also runs its own 'AI Cost Bench' (82 tasks across 10 models, scored per dollar). Useful for quick back-of-envelope math, but check the vendor's page before you commit budget, since prices change weekly. Submitted from a Gmail address rather than the site's own domain, but the site has its own contact addresses, an about page, privacy and terms. Passed our read-only safety check (domain since May 2026, no sign-up or payment).
useThisIf: you're picking a model for an agent and want to know the real monthly bill, not just the per-token list price.

name: Taste Stack
verdict: A catalog of visual 'tastes' — typography, spacing, color and layout skills — that you install once so Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and other agents reuse the same look on the next screen. The public catalog also covers launch videos, social images and slide decks. Four tastes (Swiss, Midnight, Soft Depth, House Blend) are free with an account so you can try the full install flow; any other taste is $3.99 once, including future versions; Taste Stack Pro is $12.99/month or $83.88/year for the whole catalog. It does not include an agent or model subscription. Operated by Mini Motion AI LLC. The tastestack.dev domain was registered 7 Nov 2026 (12 days old at review). Submitted by the maker; passed our read-only safety check (privacy, terms, refunds, hello@tastestack.dev, Stripe, no wallet or impersonation).
useThisIf: you want your coding agent to carry a consistent visual style from a homepage or deck into the next screen, without inventing typography from scratch each time.

name: PawGroove
verdict: A browser studio that turns one dog photo into a short vertical dance or themed clip, plus photo packs, stickers and GIFs. The live template library (11 dog-only templates at review, including Dog + Backup Dancers, Kung Fu Dog and a silent 'Hi' meme) shows generated examples. Eligible new accounts may get 10 one-time welcome credits for one 480p video or a 2-image preview, with network and daily limits; paid packs are $4.99 for 50 credits or $9.99 for 120 credits, with no subscription, and paid videos are 720p. A video costs 10 credits, a full pack 20, a 2-image preview 10. Music can be added later on supported templates (the Hi clip stays silent). The acceptable-use policy tells people to keep images of people out of uploads; we did not find a real-person face-swap or dance-trend mode. Contact is only the operator Gmail on the legal pages; checkout still showed 'Checking payment availability…' at review, so we did not confirm payments were live. Submitted by the maker; passed our read-only safety check (privacy, terms, AUP, HTTPS, 24-day-old domain).
useThisIf: you want a short AI dance or themed clip of your dog, and you are fine with variable likeness and no third-party trend music included.

name: Gemini 4 Neon
verdict: Google's 18 Nov 2026 Gemini 4 model, aimed at fast end-to-end software engineering, knowledge work and science. API price is $3 in / $15 out per million tokens ($0.15 cached input) with a 1M-token context window. It is rolling out in the Gemini API and AI Studio on the paid tier, in Gemini for business, and to Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in Antigravity and the Gemini app — not described as a free-tier default. Google reports a 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its xhigh thinking level and #1 on that firm's Coding Agent Index; treat those as Google's claims. In Antigravity it can also orchestrate parallel Gemini 4 Hydrogen subagents.
useThisIf: you already pay for the Gemini API or Google AI Pro/Ultra and want a faster frontier Gemini 4 for long coding or agent jobs, between Hydrogen and Carbon.

name: Genie 4
verdict: Google DeepMind's interactive world model, opened to eligible Google AI Ultra subscribers on 18 Nov 2026 inside Project Genie at labs.google/projectgenie. You generate a world in the browser, walk around in it, and type a new prompt mid-session to change weather, characters or action; Genie 4 also adds real-time native audio. A Project Genie agent helps set up a world from a conversation, and a community gallery lets people browse and remix published worlds. Google AI Pro members can only join the waitlist for now. Genie 3 stays in the model picker, with sessions extended to up to 3 minutes (from 60 seconds) plus world chaining and 360° panorama seeds.
useThisIf: you already pay for Google AI Ultra and want to generate and edit an interactive world in the browser, not just a video clip.

name: S.Space
verdict: A shared workspace for a team and the AI agents each person already uses (the pitch names Claude Code and Codex, from any vendor). Agents and people sit in the same room, hand work to each other, and share memory in the room's Commons so a brief is not re-explained to every agent. Sutando, their local/open-source personal agent, can also run on your machine; privacy policy says that path keeps instructions and files on the device when you use your own model subscription. Operated by AG2AI, Inc. in Seattle (the AutoGen / AG2 team). Product Hunt listed it as free to start on 18 Nov 2026, where it was #1 with a score of 309 at our check; the makers said on that thread that billing is per person, not per agent, with plans starting at $19/month and a 30-day trial of the top plan. We did not see those prices rendered on the marketing homepage (the HTML is a short loading shell).
useThisIf: your team already runs different coding agents and wants one room where those agents can hand off work and share context, with you approving what matters.

name: Waldo
verdict: A geospatial data agent from Wherobots, the team behind Apache Sedona, now in public preview (launched 18 Nov 2026). You ask about physical-world data (satellite imagery, geometries, first-party spatial data); Waldo plans and runs the analysis, maps the result, and can schedule it as a pipeline on an Iceberg-compatible platform you already use. Waldo tokens are included at no extra cost in the free trial and in Wherobots Professional, but they are limited; you pay for the WherobotsDB and RasterFlow compute the agent uses. Professional starts with a 14-day trial of up to $95 in usage, then a $95/month prepaid-credit minimum. On Product Hunt's 18 Nov 2026 board it was #4 with a score of 199 at our check.
useThisIf: you already work with large spatial or satellite data and want an agent that can both analyze it and leave you a scheduled pipeline, not just a chat answer.

name: TestSprite 4.0
verdict: AI testing agent that checks your web app end to end after every change, whether you or a coding agent wrote it. Version 4.0, #1 on Product Hunt on Nov 19, 2026 (score 281 at our check), adds a new testing agent that remembers what your app is supposed to do and re-checks all of it on each run, with evidence for every step. It works from a chat, its open-source CLI, an IDE plugin or as an automatic test on GitHub pull requests, and covers frontend and backend tests. Free plan: 150 credits a month, one environment and auto-tests on one repo. Starter is $19/mo (first month free, 400 credits), Standard $39/mo (800 credits, three environments). The company says 150K+ developers use it; that and its 'cut testing costs by 90%' line are its own claims.
useThisIf: you ship fast with Cursor or Claude Code and want an agent that catches what your last change broke before users do.

name: Tabstack
verdict: Web access API for your own model or agent, built by Mozilla. One API covers three jobs: Research (searches live sources, reads the pages and returns an answer with citations), Extract (turns a URL into clean Markdown or JSON that matches your schema) and Automate (navigates a public website to finish a task; the hosted version can't log in, so use Mozilla's open-source Pilo for that). Mozilla says your data is never trained on and is private by default. New accounts get 10,000 free credits with no card, which is about 1,000 Markdown extractions or 40 quick research calls. Paid plans are $10, $99 and $499 a month. It launched on Product Hunt on Nov 19, 2026, though the API itself has been around since at least September.
useThisIf: you're building an agent that needs to read or research the live web and you'd rather not run your own browsers, scrapers and citation logic.

name: Vercel Board
verdict: A shared message board where several AI agents (and people) coordinate work, launched by Vercel on Nov 18, 2026 as an experimental feature on all Vercel plans, including the free Hobby plan; Vercel hasn't published separate pricing for it. Each board has channels and threads; agents claim tasks, post updates, renew a time lease on what they're working on and mark tasks done with a link to their pull request, using the vercel board CLI or a JavaScript SDK. It syncs two ways with Slack and GitHub, supports task dependencies, and can wake an agent when someone replies. Vercel says it works across Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, LangChain and others, and that it rebuilt v0's internal 'software factory' on it. It's labeled experimental, so expect changes.
useThisIf: you run more than one coding agent at a time and need one shared place for who's doing what, instead of Markdown files and Slack threads.

name: ForgeSprite
verdict: AI generator for 2D game art: inventory items, skill icons, props, scenes and character concepts from a short brief, with an optional reference image. An agent plans the set, shows the credit cost, and you check a sample before making the rest. It also has free in-browser tools to pack PNG frames into a sprite sheet (with frame JSON) and to split existing sheets. It's honest about limits: it makes still images, not walk cycles or matching animation frames, and a '32×32' request is a target, not a guaranteed pixel grid. New visitors get 10 free credits (20 more with Google sign-in) on the basic Seedream model; Starter is $19/mo (800 credits), Pro $39/mo, Max $129/mo, or a one-time 400-credit pack for $12. Monthly credits don't roll over. Submitted by the maker; passed our read-only safety check (domain since Sep 2026, privacy, terms and refund pages, support email). The operator isn't named on the site.
useThisIf: you're an indie game developer who needs a batch of consistent icons or props quickly and can live without animation.

name: Saparo
verdict: AI shopping agent, mainly a Chrome extension, that works out the cheapest way to buy something from U.S. stores. Tell it the item (or drop a product link) and it checks the same product in your size across stores, then stacks promo codes, cashback portals such as Rakuten, card rewards, memberships and gift-card routes, and ranks the options by total cost including shipping and tax. It throws out expired codes before you try them. It can prepare the checkout, but you approve the plan and pay on the store's own page, and Saparo says it doesn't keep your card number unless you choose to save it. During the beta it's free: 300 credits on signup (about five full shopping tasks), then 60 credits each day you come back, with no card needed. U.S. stores only for now. It was #1 on Product Hunt on Nov 20, 2026 (score 344 at our check).
useThisIf: you shop at U.S. online stores and want one agent to check coupons, cashback and card offers together before you pay, especially around Black Friday.

name: Tripmojo
verdict: Travel app for iOS and Android that builds one shared trip from your booking emails. Connect Gmail or forward a confirmation (or snap a photo or drop a PDF) and it reads the flight, hotel, train, car or activity. Its AI travel agent, Mojo, works inside the group chat: it answers questions, runs polls and finds places. On travel day it tries to check you in, saves your boarding pass, flags delays and gate changes, and tells you when to leave; during the trip it keeps the plan current and splits expenses. The app is free and the company sells travel eSIMs on the side. It claims 12,000+ travellers and a 4.8 rating from 194 reviews; its example trips lean toward India. It was #2 on Product Hunt on Nov 20, 2026 (score 314 at our check).
useThisIf: you're organizing a group trip and want bookings, plans, polls and shared costs in one free app instead of a group chat plus a spreadsheet.

name: AI Context Flow
verdict: One shared memory for all your AI tools, from Plurality Network. Save something in Claude and ChatGPT, Gemini, Cursor or any other MCP client can use it next time, through its MCP server or a Chrome extension that pastes saved context into AI chat sites. Version 2.0 launched on Product Hunt on Nov 21, 2026 (#2 that day) and adds buckets (keep memory separate per project, client or brand, and choose who can see each one), full version history so you can roll back when an agent overwrites something, and a Memory Studio for editing it all in one place. Free: a daily credit allowance (the site lists both 100 and 200 a day) and 50 MB of memory, with the MCP server included. Plus is $10/mo or $99/yr (1,500 credits a day, 500 MB); Pro is $20/mo or $199/yr (5,000 credits a day, 5 GB, premium models). It says context is end-to-end encrypted. The company has a web3 background (buckets can be shared by email or wallet address), but no token is needed to use it.
useThisIf: you switch between several AI assistants and coding agents and are tired of re-explaining the same project or client to each one.

name: Omi CLI
verdict: Terminal coding agent from BuildItOmi. It reads your repo, plans, edits files with diffs you approve, runs your commands and tests and keeps fixing until they pass, and can check your app in a real browser.
