Parallel subagents work in separate git worktrees and are merged back file by file (conflicts get standard markers, never a silent winner); background agents keep going after you close the terminal, and cloud agents can open pull requests. 'Auto' picks a model for each turn from 13 mostly cheaper models (DeepSeek, Gemini Flash, GLM, gpt-oss and others), or you can bring your own key or run a local model through Ollama. A --sandbox mode keeps commands inside the project with no network on macOS and Linux. Free plan with limits that refill every 5 hours and weekly; Pro $20/mo, Pro+ $60/mo, Max $200/mo. Launched on Product Hunt on Nov 22, 2026 (#8 that day). Frontier models like Claude and GPT aren't in the included list.
useThisIf: you want a Claude Code-style terminal agent that runs on cheaper models, with diff approval and worktree subagents, and a free tier to try it.

name: Motionflare
verdict: AI video generator for brands that starts from a public website URL or a one-sentence idea. In Motion mode it builds a motion-graphics video from the site's real logo, colors, copy and screenshots, with a generated score and optional narration, and you change it in chat; paid plans go up to 10–90 seconds. Film mode (open to every account since Oct 9, 2026) writes a live-action commercial of 5–45 seconds in 16:9 or 9:16, at up to 4K, with voiceover, sound and music. It is not an avatar-presenter tool or a timeline editor, and it is not Motion by Mosaic (motion.so). Free: 6 credits once, enough to generate and preview one watermarked video or film of up to 10 seconds; exporting a 1080p or 4K file needs a subscription or any credit pack (packs start at $15, no subscription, credits do not expire). Pro is $29/month for 100 credits; Max $99/month for 500; Ultra $950/month for 5,000. As of Nov 24, 2026, the first month of Pro or Max is 50% off until Dec 1, 2026, 11:59 PM Pacific. It was #3 on Product Hunt on Nov 23, 2026 (score 234 at our check).
useThisIf: you need a launch, demo or brand film from a product page and would rather paste a URL than storyboard or edit a timeline.

name: Modem
verdict: Customer-feedback graph that watches support inboxes, team chat, community posts, sales calls and an API feed, groups repeated concerns into one topic, and links each topic to the issues and pull requests that fix it. It can alert the team, open a ticket, or hand the context to a coding agent in Claude Code, Cursor or Devin, and it tries to close the loop with the customer when the fix ships. There's a Modem agent in Slack, Discord and the web, plus an MCP server and a REST API. Free: $0, 2,500 events and 1,000 agent credits a month, 60 days of history, unlimited users; paid plans also have a 14-day trial with no card. Startup is $80/month (15,000 events, 10,000 agent credits, 180 days, public X monitoring). Scale is $250/month (60,000 events, 40,000 credits, one year of history, Gong and Fathom calls). Enterprise is custom (SAML/SCIM, SLA). An event is a signal Modem runs inference on, such as a Slack message or a support ticket. It was #4 on Product Hunt on Nov 23, 2026 (score 195 at our check).
useThisIf: customer complaints land in several channels and you want one place that groups them, ties them to the fix, and follows up when it ships.

name: Polylane
verdict: AI SRE from Coreplane that watches logs, metrics and traces, opens an issue when something drifts from the learned baseline, investigates across code, deploys and telemetry, and opens a pull request with a fix. It also scans active, deployed GitHub and GitLab repos for known CVEs, checks pull requests for production impact before you merge, and can group overnight alerts and investigate real incidents. You can ask it from Claude Code, Cursor, Codex or any MCP client, from Slack, or over a REST API (reads are unlimited on every plan). Free forever: one cloud account, one team member, 10 impact assessments a month, and a monthly credit allowance, with no card. Paid plans start at Starter $80/month or $64/month billed yearly (16× Free's credits, two cloud accounts), then Team $200, Business $500, Scale $800, Premium $2,000 and Ultimate $5,000 per month (yearly prices are 20% less). Enterprise is custom (bring your own model key or cloud); a human answers at boris@coreplane.ai. It was #6 on Product Hunt on Nov 23, 2026 (score 126 at our check).
useThisIf: you want an agent watching production and opening a documented PR when it thinks it has a fix, and you're willing to review those PRs before they merge.

name: Chat with Work
verdict: AI work bots, hosted in the EU, that you describe in a sentence and that run across 1,920+ integrations (mail, calendar, CRM, helpdesk and more). They start work on their own and pause for your approval when something would go out or change a record; every question and approval lands in one inbox. The company positions this against Claude Duet (US only), ChatGPT's scheduled tasks (not on Pro or Plus in Europe) and Gemini's Tasks (not in Europe). Every login gets 300 trial credits once, for every model, with no plan and no card. When credits run out the answer stops; it never bills extra. Personal plans (VAT included, priced for a one-person org): €20/month for 900 credits, €100/month for 4,500, or €200/month for 10,000; a year costs ten months. Team plans are €25, €125 or €250 per person per month plus VAT, with the same credit tiers pooled across the team; guests are free. Top-up is 400 credits for €10 (VAT included), valid 3 years (12 months for businesses). Bigger models use more credits per answer. It was #8 on Product Hunt on Nov 23, 2026 (score 118 at our check).
useThisIf: you're in Europe and want bots that work across your existing tools and wait for you to approve anything that sends or changes data.

name: Hydrilla
verdict: AI 3D workspace that turns a text prompt or a reference image into a segmented model with UVs and PBR maps (base color, roughness, metalness, normals), via its BlueFox model from Hawan Research Labs. You can preview under lighting, edit logical parts in Hydrilla Studio, generate from a Blender add-on, and export GLB, FBX, OBJ or USDZ for Unity, Unreal, Godot and AR. Hydrilla Agent can build a scene in Blender from a chat description; it asks before a generation spends credits, and you can bring your own model key. The company's own FAQ says assets that sit close to camera still need an artist's pass. Free is $0 with 100 credits a month (a default-quality model from text costs 45 credits, from an image 30). Starter is $5/month for 900 credits; Pro is $12/month for 3,000 credits and includes the REST API. Hourly ($3/month) and Hourly Pro ($8/month) give the same credit counts as Starter and Pro but only in a chosen daily window. A 14-day trial of any paid plan needs a card; unused credits do not roll over. The company is Hydrilla AI Private Limited in Tirupati, India (founders@hydrilla.ai). It was #9 on Product Hunt on Nov 23, 2026 (score 107 at our check).
useThisIf: you need a starting 3D asset or a Blender scene from a prompt or photo, and you're ready to clean up anything that will be seen up close.

name: Granular
verdict: Desktop workspace (Mac, and Windows in beta) for running several AI agents in parallel, with real terminals, project files, a live preview, a project brain and boss/worker agents. You bring your own Claude, Codex or Gemini subscription or API key; Granular does not mark those tokens up. It is not a model: without an AI connection the agent cannot work. Free includes 2 projects, up to 4 sessions each, one boss agent and two worker agents, and up to 3 published links. Pro lifts those limits: $12.99/month, $129/year (about $10.75/month), or $259 once for a lifetime license, usable on 2 computers, with a 30-day money-back guarantee (email hello@granular.build; the AI Add-on and credit packs are not covered). An optional Granular Hosted AI Add-on bills separately and works on Free or Pro: the same hosted models from 9 providers, with Base at $20/month for 1,600 credits, Plus $50/month for 4,000, or Max $100/month for 8,000. Those monthly credits refill every 30 days and do not carry over; one-time packs are $10 for 800 credits or $25 for 2,000 and last until you use them. Image, video and voice add-ons are listed as coming soon. It was #2 on Product Hunt on Nov 24, 2026.
useThisIf: you want a visual desktop workspace where several coding or general agents can work in your folders, and you already pay for Claude, Codex or Gemini (or are willing to buy Granular's hosted credits).

name: Clam
verdict: A permission layer between Gmail and AI agents. You write plain-English rules for what each agent may read, draft or send; Clam compiles them into Cedar policies and checks every request. Each agent gets its own Shell, a slice of the inbox rather than the whole mailbox, and Clam logs every allowed or blocked action. It does not store email content, and Google tokens stay with Clerk, its auth provider. Connectors are offered for Claude, ChatGPT, Hermes, Gemini, Muse and Grok over MCP. Gmail only, for now. A 14-day free trial of Starter needs no credit card; Starter is then $2.99/month for one mailbox and one Shell. Pro is $6.99/month for 10 Shells per mailbox, 90 days of history, 4,000 classified emails a month, plus the audit log, approvals and office hours. Sign up for annual billing before the end of 2026 and the first year is $29.90 on Starter or $69.90 on Pro. If the trial ends with no card on file, Shells stop answering and your connection is kept for 30 days. CASA AL1 was validated in Oct 2026; SOC 2 was still in audit as of our check, expected Dec 2026. It was #3 on Product Hunt on Nov 24, 2026 (the product was introduced on Nov 11).
useThisIf: you want an agent to help with Gmail but will not hand it the whole inbox, and you are willing to write rules for each agent.

name: Claude Ship
verdict: Anthropic's beta for GitHub pull requests, available on Claude Team and Enterprise plans. After a PR opens, Code Review uses multiple agents to flag issues (ranked Important, Nit or Pre-existing), with quick, standard or deep review levels and a REVIEW.md file to tune what gets flagged. PR Steward, also in beta, works on review feedback, failing checks and merge conflicts in the cloud; it can start on its own or only when someone comments @claude steward, and it is designed to leave approving and merging to your team. Claude Approvals reads a policy file in the repo and can approve routine changes where that policy allows; Anthropic recommends starting in observe mode, where it posts a decision but approves nothing. This is not a general coding agent like Claude Code: it automates review, fixes and policy-based approval on GitHub PRs. There is no separate public price; you connect a repo and set a monthly spend limit for Code Review. It was featured on Product Hunt on Nov 24, 2026.
useThisIf: your team is already on Claude Team or Enterprise and wants Claude to review, fix and (where your policy allows) approve GitHub pull requests, with a human still in the loop for merges.

name: MAGI-2
verdict: Sand.ai's flagship video model, launched Nov 24, 2026: a 480B-parameter mixture-of-experts (~28B active) trained on 4T tokens. It generates up to 30 seconds of native 1080p, 25 fps video with synchronized audio, including lip-synced dialogue, foley, ambience and music, in six aspect ratios. A request can take up to 20 references (10 images, 5 videos and 5 audio clips), and the model supports timeline/shot-cut control and editing of existing video. As of Nov 25, 2026 it is available only on Higgsfield and the Higgsfield API, at USD 0.08 per second of requested video (a default 5-second clip is $0.40), with generated audio included; one MAGI-2 generation can run at a time per account. Higgsfield also sells credit plans (Starter is $19/month for 270 credits; Plus and Ultra list prices and a Black Friday sale, ending Nov 26, 2026 00:00 UTC, are on higgsfield.ai/pricing). Sand.ai says an open-source release and a technical report will follow. A smaller MAGI-2 Preview (~114B) came out in August 2026.
useThisIf: you want longer 1080p clips with native sound and multiple image, video or audio references, and you are willing to run them through Higgsfield.

name: Google Antigravity
verdict: Google's agent-first development platform: a desktop app for running local agents in parallel, a terminal CLI, an agentic IDE with IDE extensions, and a Python SDK, including browser-in-the-loop checks and scheduled tasks. Individual is $0/month, with a weekly quota and Gemini 4 Hydrogen, Gemini 3.8 Flash, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Claude Opus 4.6 and GPT-OSS-120b. The pricing page says several of those models leave on 30 Nov 2026. Google AI Pro and Ultra add quotas that refresh every 5 hours and, on paid plans, Gemini 4 Neon, Gemini 4 Carbon, Orchestrator and Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5. Organizations can use it through Google Cloud Gemini Enterprise from $30 per seat per month, or pay-as-you-go.
useThisIf: you want Google's agent-first app, CLI and IDE, on the free Individual tier or on a paid Google AI plan that includes Gemini 4 Neon.

name: Macswarm
verdict: Cloud macOS virtual machines (Pods) on Apple silicon for Claude Code and Codex agents that need Xcode and iOS Simulators. Each developer gets one Pod. Their agents share it, with two xcodebuild slots and a small pool of pre-booted Simulators, and the Pod is destroyed 10 minutes after the last session. Uncommitted work is pushed to a rescue branch. You bring your own Claude or OpenAI account; Macswarm bills Pod-hours, not model tokens. Free is 3 Pod-hours once, with no card. Pro is $99/month for 300 Pod-hours, then $0.40 per extra hour. Team is $399/month for 1,500, then $0.30. Enterprise starts at $3,000/month.
useThisIf: you run Claude Code or Codex from the web, Slack or a Linux cloud session and need a real macOS and Xcode environment to build and check iOS apps.

name: Vertov
verdict: Browser and Chrome-extension screen recorder for teams and agents. You can record without an account, cut the video by deleting words in the transcript, zoom or blur a detail, draft a procedure from the transcript, import Loom videos, and hand a recording to an agent over MCP or the API. Plans are priced by stored video hours, and members and viewers are free. Free keeps 180 minutes. Pro is $9/month for 25 hours, Team is $29/month for 125 hours, and Business starts at $99/month for 500 hours. The core is AGPL-3.0. The hosted app adds sharing and a choice of US or EU storage.
useThisIf: you want Loom-style walkthroughs priced by stored hours rather than seats, and a way for an agent to read a bug recording or upload proof.

name: CADProps Connector for Claude
verdict: Remote MCP connector at https://www.cadprops.com/api/v1/mcp and a browser CAD viewer. You upload one file through a one-time link so Claude can read dimensions, volume and surface area, and ask for an STL or GLB conversion. CADProps accepts 92 or more extensions, including STEP, IGES, SolidWorks, CATIA, STL and DWG/DXF. Exact B-Rep measurements and approximate mesh results are labeled separately. Guest inspection needs no account: 95 MiB, deleted about an hour after upload. A free account allows 15 uploads a day and 200 MB, plus one free 7-day share link. Conversions and Pro share links use points, sold as 20 points for $6 or 80 points for $15, paid once.
useThisIf: you work with STEP, SolidWorks or IGES parts and want Claude to inspect geometry and measurements without a desktop CAD install.

name: Open Agent API
verdict: Apache-2.0 self-hosted gateway that turns local coding CLIs, including Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, OpenCode and Qoder, and local model runners such as Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp and vLLM, into stateful API endpoints. Existing OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini SDK calls can target an agent by changing the base URL. It keeps project memory in SQLite with FTS5 and pauses sensitive shell or write steps at a durable approval checkpoint. It ships as a CLI, a Docker Compose service and an Electron app, and binds to localhost by default.
useThisIf: you want existing OpenAI, Anthropic or Gemini SDK code to call a tool-using coding agent, with approval gates and local execution.

name: OpenLegion
verdict: Hosted agent harness for multi-tenant SaaS and AI apps, in private beta. You define an agent and its tools in code. OpenLegion runs one isolated workspace per end customer, checks tool calls against policy, pauses for human approval, meters credits against a per-customer cap, keeps secrets in a vault, and sends signed receipts and webhooks. An idle workspace uses no credits. Partner pricing is shared at onboarding. No public price was listed at our check on 25 Nov 2026, and the company says it does not claim SOC 2 or ISO 27001 yet.
useThisIf: you want customer-facing agents inside a multi-tenant product and do not want to build tenant isolation, approval queues and spend caps yourself.

name: Spreadsheet to App
verdict: AI builder that turns an Excel workbook, a CSV or a Google Sheet into a hosted web app and keeps Google Sheets as the database. Studio shows a private preview, the generated code, and the five most recent checkpoints before you publish. Formula cells stay read-only, uploaded Excel and CSV files do not keep syncing with the original file, and the data gateway does not offer per-row permissions. Free is $0 for 1 app and 1 seat, with a limited monthly AI allowance and no card. Basic is $25/month for 5 apps and 2 seats. Pro is $75/month for 20 apps, 3 seats and 5 times Basic's weekly AI allowance. Business is $125/month for 20 apps, 3 seats and no AI allowance cap. Extra seats are $5 per person per month.
useThisIf: your team already runs inventory, a tracker or a lightweight CRM in Google Sheets or Excel and wants a web UI without moving that data into a SQL database.

name: ReelSDK
verdict: AI generator for vertical shorts, with a REST API and a local MCP server (bitgate/reelsdk-mcp) for Claude Code, Cursor and n8n. A topic, a clip or photos becomes a 9:16 MP4 with a script, scene images, voiceover, burned-in captions and music. A short up to 60 seconds is $0.30, and up to 90 seconds is $0.45. The browser tool makes 2 shorts a day with no account, and a signup includes $0.50 of credit with no card. A $4 starter pack covers 13 shorts. Creator is $9/month for 36 shorts ($0.25 each). Build is $29/month for 120 shorts. Scale is $99/month for 430 shorts. A short that fails is not charged.
useThisIf: you want pay-as-you-go vertical video, from a browser, a REST call or an MCP coding agent.

name: QuestStudio
verdict: Creative workspace for product images, short promo videos, voiceovers and music, all drawing on one credit balance. The studio lists models including FLUX 2 Pro, Seedream 5 Pro, Nano Banana 2, Nano Banana Pro, Veo 3.1, Seedance 2.5, Kling 4.0, Runway Gen-4 Turbo, Lyria 3 and MiniMax Speech 2.8. A free account includes 5 FLUX Schnell images in total, with no card. A 7-day trial with 100 credits requires a card. Starter, Pro and Studio are monthly credit plans. Their dollar prices were not on the page checked on 25 Nov 2026.
useThisIf: you make product shots and promo clips and want image, video, voice and music models on one credit balance, with brand kits.

name: Tiquo
verdict: Hospitality operating platform that combines POS, reservations, memberships, kitchen display, inventory, Stripe payments and CRM for restaurants, hotels, spas and other venues. Tiquo AI answers questions about your numbers and suggests customer segments and campaign drafts. Starter is £59 per product or service sublocation per month for venues under £200k a year, with card rates from 1.9% + £0.22. Launch is £300, with card rates from 1.7% + £0.22. Scale is £400, with card rates from 1.2% + £0.18. Enterprise is custom. There is no free tier.
useThisIf: you run a restaurant, hotel, spa or venue and want POS, bookings, memberships and AI reporting in one system.

name: AICertMock
verdict: Independent practice exams for Anthropic's Claude Certified Architect (CCAR-F) exam. A free 10-question diagnostic needs no login. It scores the five domains and explains the first five questions. Starter is $4.99 once, for mock exam 1 and the rest of the diagnostic explanations. Pro Pass is $9.99 once, for all three 60-question mocks (180 questions) and a wrong-answer drill. AICertMock says it is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Anthropic. Unused passes can be refunded within 7 days, or within 14 days in the EU and EEA.
useThisIf: you are preparing for the CCAR-F exam and want scenario questions mapped to its five domains.

name: MyClaw 3.0
verdict: Managed cloud platform for always-on AI teammate teams, launched as MyClaw 3.0 on Product Hunt on Nov 25, 2026. You pick an agent engine (OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, Pi, Claude Code, Codex or DeepSeek Harness), assign a role, tools and skills, and run it on a cloud computer that keeps working after you close your laptop. Agents share one memory, and you can assign work from the web, Slack, Telegram or WhatsApp. The site lists 50+ models and a pay-as-you-go data router so you do not manage extra API keys for search and web data. Pro is $20/month or $17/month billed yearly ($200/year) for 4,000 credits, 4 vCPU, 8 GB RAM and 80 GB storage. Max is $40/month or $34/month yearly ($400/year) for 8,000 credits and 8 vCPU. ULTRA is $200/month or $167/month yearly ($2,000/year) for 40,000 credits and 16 vCPU. Enterprise is custom. No free plan was listed on the pricing page checked on Nov 26, 2026. Cancel anytime; contact is contact@myclaw.ai.
useThisIf: you want a managed, always-on cloud computer for a mix of coding and work agents, with shared memory, and you are ready to pay from the Pro plan.

name: Airbot
verdict: Airspeed's AI chief of staff, launched on Product Hunt on Nov 25, 2026. It watches CRM, email, calendar, Slack and call tools, then texts you first in WhatsApp or iMessage with a priority and a drafted next step for you to approve. The company site lists connections including Salesforce, HubSpot, Gong, Gmail, Outlook, Google Calendar, Slack and Granola. On the day of the Product Hunt launch the product site said doors were opening soon and that Product Hunt visitors could skip the waitlist. No public price was listed on airbots.ai or the Airspeed Airbot page when checked on Nov 26, 2026. Privacy and terms are on goairspeed.com.
useThisIf: you already live in WhatsApp or iMessage and want a sales or pipeline assistant that brings you drafted follow-ups instead of another dashboard.

name: Hai
verdict: Independent AI phone-call assistant, launched on Product Hunt on Nov 25, 2026 by a maker in Japan. You ask your existing assistant to book a restaurant, clinic or salon; Hai shows a plan, waits for your yes, places the call in the local language, identifies itself as an AI, and reports back in your chat. Official setup is an MCP server at https://haicall.in/mcp for Muse, ChatGPT (Pro or Business, with a regional limit noted for the EEA, the UK and Switzerland), Grok Bot, Claude and Claude Code. Nothing to install. The site says it is in testing: new accounts are approved by hand, and until then your assistant will say you are on the waitlist. No public price was listed when checked on Nov 26, 2026. Privacy and terms are on the site.
useThisIf: you need a real phone booking made for you from chat, and you are willing to wait for a manually approved account.

name: Koed
verdict: Free, Apache-2.0 local-first memory layer for coding agents, launched on Product Hunt on Nov 25, 2026. Koed captures useful context from agent sessions and recalls it later so Claude Code, Codex and Pi can reuse project decisions instead of rediscovering them. The desktop app is at v1.2.0 for macOS on Apple silicon and Linux as an x64 AppImage; Windows is listed as coming soon, with WSL pointed at the server install. You can also run curl -fsSL https://koed.ai/install | bash (Python 3) or build from https://github.com/koed-labs/koed. The site's Free tier is the self-hosted memory loop. Pro (hosted embeddings and recall on any device) and team sharing are listed as coming soon. The site quotes a 20-task Terminal-Bench 4 comparison on GPT-6 Luna; treat those figures as the vendor's own benchmark.
useThisIf: you want an on-device, open-source memory layer for Claude Code, Codex or Pi, and you can run it on macOS Apple silicon or Linux.

name: Canva MCP
verdict: Canva's official remote MCP server for AI assistants, launched on Product Hunt on Nov 25, 2026. Assistants can create and edit Canva designs, search the library, manage assets and brand kits, add comments, and export to formats including PDF, PNG, JPG, PPTX and MP4. The documented server is at https://api.canva.com/connect/v1/mcp, with per-user OAuth. Canva's developer docs are aimed at IT admins and teams building assistants; they also point personal users to Canva's AI Connector help. No separate MCP price was listed on the docs page checked on Nov 26, 2026, and access still depends on a Canva account and Canva's developer terms.
useThisIf: you want Claude, ChatGPT or another assistant to make an editable Canva design you can open and finish in Canva, rather than a one-off image file.

name: Sandscale
verdict: Cloud sandboxes for AI coding agents: each run gets its own microVM (Firecracker), the network stays off until you allow it, and every step can go in an audit log. There is an SDK (@sandscale/sdk), an MCP server at https://mcp.sandscale.dev/mcp, workspaces, snapshots, and optional object storage. Paused and idle time does not count toward hours. Free is $0 for 100 awake vCPU-hours a month, 3 boxes at once, 5 GB storage and up to 2 vCPU per box, one Free account per person. Pro is $20/month billed yearly or $25/month, for 1,500 hours, up to 30 boxes and up to 16 vCPU, with usage beyond the plan at $0.05 per awake vCPU-hour or $10 per 500-hour pack. Team is $40 per member per month billed yearly or $48 monthly, for 2,000 pooled hours per member, plus SSO, roles and audit export. Enterprise can run in your AWS account. The sandscale.dev domain was registered 16 Nov 2026 (10 days old at review). Submitted by the maker; passed our read-only safety check (HTTPS, privacy, terms, contact, DPA and subprocessors, no wallet or impersonation).
useThisIf: you want each coding-agent run in an isolated microVM, with the network off by default and an audit log, and you are comfortable using a newly launched host.

name: AI Text Watermark Checker
verdict: In-browser checker for hidden characters in pasted text: zero-width spaces, byte-order marks, unusual spaces and look-alike letters. Scan and Strip run in the tab and stay free; the site is explicit that this does not detect statistical watermarks such as textGrain, Claude's watermark or SynthID-Text, because those live in word choice.
